episodes.title: Lighthouse
episodes.blurb: The diagnosis, the guns, the road north.

episodes.title: Highway 17
episodes.blurb: White River, Thunder Bay, an ambush in the snow.

episodes.title: Gold Country
episodes.blurb: Red Lake. The hospital, the museum, Level 9.

episodes.title: The Ice Road
episodes.blurb: McKenzie Island and the man who dug it.

episodes.title: Starratt-Olsen
episodes.blurb: Amma on the radio. A ghost town at midnight.

panel.name: Nila's blood panel
panel.desc: One unnamed compound the lab called an artefact. Preethi says it isn't.

jonahWater.name: Jonah's answer
jonahWater.desc: "I never brought you water." Someone else left those bottles at Pike Point.

label.name: Northstar shipping label
label.desc: NORTHSTAR BIOLOGICS — HX-7 — HAYDEN DEEP, RED LAKE, ON. From Victor's fireproof safe.

delivery.name: GH-01 delivery note
delivery.desc: "24 × spring water, 1 L. Pike Point. Attn: GH-01." The week Nila hid there.

guns.name: Rocco's guns
guns.desc: Pump shotgun, M4, two Desert Eagles. Illegal. Bought under the Ambassador Bridge.

ivyMap.name: Ivy's surface map
ivyMap.desc: Gatehouse, office, loading dock, and a freight elevator that goes deeper than the mine maps say.

profile.name: Dr. Okafor's profile
profile.desc: A collector who needs control. A voyeur who needs an audience. "He'll want you in the room."

dunnName.name: Constable Rachel Dunn
dunnName.desc: OPP, Red Lake. "Honest. Too honest for her own good."

convoy.name: Thursday convoy
convoy.desc: Northstar trucks run up Highway 105 every Thursday night. Fuel stop at Ear Falls.

gift.name: Welcome gift
gift.desc: A shed lancehead skin and a photo of Nila asleep, taken inside her hospital room. "Welcome to my town."

panels5.name: Five blood panels
panels5.desc: Nila and four dead Northstar workers share one peptide. Nila is about three weeks behind the last man.

hayden.name: The Hayden family
hayden.desc: Prospectors in 1934. Hayden Deep, 1946–1991. Engineer R. Hayden went south in 1974. Mark Hayden came home in 2015.

robert.name: "Old Robert"
robert.desc: Mark's father. "Must be ninety if he's a day." Some say he lives out past the Burn with his son.

level9.name: "Level 9"
level9.desc: A gold specimen with a hidden second tag. Public mine maps show only six levels.

sullyMap.name: Sully's 1974 map
sullyMap.desc: Levels 6 to 9, and a forgotten ventilation raise that comes up in the bush near Madsen.

farm.name: Venom farm photos
farm.desc: Hundreds of golden lanceheads in heated tanks on Level 9. Robotic arms milking venom.

gh01.name: Subject GH-01 file
gh01.desc: Nila. "Route: drinking water. Pike Point." In Hades's hand: "Keep her alive until the brother comes. — M.H."

rl.name: Subjects RL-01 to RL-04
rl.desc: The four dead Red Lake workers. Joe Keeper was RL-03.

cure.name: HX-7C
cure.desc: The antidote. "Three doses. Stored at the house vault. Access: M.H. only."

thermal.name: Thermal image
thermal.desc: One heat source in 400 km² north-west of the Burn: a house. Behind it, something very hot.

portraits.name: The portrait gallery
portraits.desc: Robert Hayden in a long coat beside the Merrow dam, 1978. A boy with a jar of snakes.

antivenom.name: Antivenom
antivenom.desc: One dose, taken from the Hayden Deep lab fridge by Preethi.

lines.text: A small studio, red ON AIR light. Nila, twenty-six, headphones on, hosting her new late show on a Windsor station.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: …and that's why you never trust a man who says he "doesn't really like music". Next up, something slow for the night shift—
She coughs. Covers her mouth. Looks at her palm. Blood. She keeps her voice perfectly steady.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: —here it is.
She presses play. The song starts. She slides off her chair onto the floor. The ON AIR light stays red.
A blur. You and Preethi running through emergency doors. Scans. Waiting rooms. Preethi in her hospital pharmacy uniform, between shifts. An oncologist, Dr. Singh, with a tablet.

lines.speaker: DR. SINGH
lines.text: It's aggressive. And it's atypical. Honestly, I've never seen a progression like this. We'll start treatment, but I won't pretend I understand it.
Preethi reads the blood panel over his shoulder. She stops on one line.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: What's this compound? It's not on any standard panel.

lines.speaker: DR. SINGH
lines.text: The lab flagged it as an artefact.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: (quietly, to you) It's not an artefact.
Amma and Appa arrive from Chennai, still in travel clothes. Amma takes Nila's hand.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Kanna… enna aachu unakku?
lines.subtitle: My dear… what happened to you?

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Onnum illa, Amma. Konjam blood, avlo dhaan.
lines.subtitle: It's nothing, Amma. Just a little blood, that's all.

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Unmaiya sollu. Evlo serious?
lines.subtitle: Tell me the truth. How serious?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Romba serious, Appa.
lines.subtitle: Very serious, Appa.

lines.text: Nila props herself up, a notepad on her knees. You and Preethi on the visitor chairs.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Okay. Treat it like a case. Exposure. Opportunity. Motive.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Exposure: Old Merrow. I dived in that water twice. But Anna, you dived too, and you're fine.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: So it's something only you had.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Pike Point. Six days in that shed. (beat) The water bottles.
She hands you her ham handheld.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Call Jonah. He's always on, after dark.

puzzle.title: Call Jonah
puzzle.prompt: Nila: "Jonah listens on 146.52, the national calling frequency. Everybody knows it."
hints: Slide slowly near the middle of the dial.

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: Pike Point, go ahead. (beat) Nila? Kid, is that you?

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Jonah. The water in the shed. Did you leave it for me?

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: I told you last year, kid. I never brought you water.
Nila lowers the radio.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Yaaro naan andha thanni kudikkanumnu nenachirukkaanga, Anna.
lines.subtitle: Someone wanted me to drink that water, Anna.

lines.text: Preethi has gone very still.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: If someone put something in it… there'd be a record. A supplier. A delivery.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Then go and find it. Greyhaven. The mill. Victor kept everything.
You and Preethi drive east on the county roads you swore you'd never drive again. Preethi reads Nila's notes by phone light.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: She wrote "GH-01" here and circled it three times.
A Tom Portons stop. Harold and June at the window table.

lines.speaker: HAROLD
lines.text: The data fella! June, it's the data fella!

lines.speaker: JUNE
lines.text: Still on decaf, Harold, don't get excited.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: (whispering) You know these people?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Long story. It involved a cat phone case.
A blackened shell behind police tape. A private guard in a hut with a space heater. Ruth, a year older, scanner on her belt, shotgun on her shoulder, meets you at the fence.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Corbin's in prison. Victor's in the ground. And nobody in this town says the name Hades out loud.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: (to Preethi) You must be the wife. He talks about you on the phone to Nila. Nauseating.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Guard changes at two-fifteen. You've got ten minutes.
Preethi climbs the water tower ladder with binoculars. You wait at the fence for her call.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: He's in the hut. Heater's on. He's watching something on his phone. Go now. Stay left, along the wall.
You cross the yard in the shadows. Halfway, Preethi's voice again, sharp:

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Stop. He's standing up.

fx.toast: Gravel crunches. The guard's flashlight swings out.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: …He's just stretching. Okay. Go.
Victor's office is a burned box open to the sky. In the corner, his fireproof safe survived, blackened but whole. A keypad. You remember this keypad. You remember his love of anniversaries.

puzzle.title: Victor's safe
puzzle.prompt: Victor's codes always remembered "the day it all began": the day he took over the mill.
hints: Month and day: 0314.

lines.text: The safe door swings open. Ash and papers. Two things matter.
A shipping label: "NORTHSTAR BIOLOGICS — HX-7 — HAYDEN DEEP, RED LAKE, ON."
A delivery note: "24 × spring water, 1 L. Pike Point. Attn: GH-01." Dated the week Nila hid there.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Anni. GH-01. It's her. She was a subject. A test subject.
Silence on the radio. Then, very tight:

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Get out. Guard's coming your way.
The flashlight passes over the ash a metre from your boots. The guard yawns, scratches, and walks back to his heater. You slip out the way you came.
The guard shouts. Before he reaches the fence, a shotgun blast booms into the sky from the road. Ruth. The guard dives for his hut. You're over the fence and gone.
The label and the note on Nila's bed tray. Nila looks stronger, the way people do when they have a job.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Red Lake. Northwestern Ontario. Gold country. End of the road. (She taps the label.) Northstar Biologics, registered 2015. Director: M. Hayden. The same Hayden from the plaque at the station. Victor's "Mark".

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: He's not hiding, Anna. He's waiting.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Then we take it to the police.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: With what? A label from a burned building. Ortiz already tried; the OPP said Greyhaven is closed. (beat) Hades has the cure. I'd bet my life on it. I am betting my life on it.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Then we go.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Then you go prepared. Kane's people shot at you in Greyhaven. Up there it'll be worse. (beat) Which brings us to the guns.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: We can buy hunting rifles, right? People up north have them.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Legally? A licence takes months: a course, a test, background checks. An M4-style rifle is prohibited in Canada, full stop. A Desert Eagle is a restricted handgun; you'd need a special licence just to drive it anywhere. Grenades, forget it.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: We don't have months, Anni. I have weeks.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: So what are you saying?

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: I studied criminals for four years. Tonight I need one. (She opens her laptop.) Rocco Delisle. Auto body shop off Wyandotte West. Charged twice, never convicted. Brings guns over the river from Detroit. I covered his second trial for a class project. I know what he sells, what he charges, and that he's terrified of court.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Nila, this is a crime.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: So is what's happening in my blood. (beat) Anni, I'll understand if you don't go.

choices.label: "Naan varen. Nee en thangachi maadhiri."
choices.sub: PREETHI: I'm coming. You're like my own little sister.

choices.label: "I'm coming. But we use them only to survive."

lines.text: Rain. The bridge's lights above, trucks rumbling across to Detroit. A grey van with its rear doors open. Rocco Delisle, fifties, leather jacket, two silent men behind him.
Nila is on the radio in your ear, from her hospital bed.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Let him talk first. He likes the sound of his own voice.

lines.speaker: ROCCO
lines.text: The radio girl's brother. She sent me a very polite message. Mentioned my court dates. Very polite.
He opens a case.

lines.speaker: ROCCO
lines.text: Pump shotgun, twelve-gauge. M4, clean, no serial. Two Desert Eagles. Ammo. Forty grand.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: He charged the last buyer twenty-two. Say twenty-five.

choices.label: "You charged the last guy twenty-two, Rocco."

lines.speaker: ROCCO
lines.text: (sighing) Your sister should be a lawyer. 26.
Preethi steps forward to inspect the weapons. She handles them like she handles a pharmacy order: everything checked, nothing assumed.

puzzle.title: Inspect the guns
puzzle.prompt: Preethi compares the two Desert Eagles side by side. One of them is wrong. What's wrong with it?

options.why: Scratches are cosmetic. It'll still fire.

options.t: The firing pin has been filed down; it won't fire
The magazine is a different colour
options.why: Aftermarket magazines are common. Not the problem.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: This one's dead, Rocco. The pin's filed.
Rocco laughs and swaps it from the van without argument.

lines.speaker: ROCCO
lines.text: Your sister said you were sharp. She didn't say it was the wife.
Headlights on the riverfront road above. A police cruiser, rolling slowly.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Patrol car, westbound. Ninety seconds. Close the doors.

choices.label: Close the van doors and stand like you're chatting
Grab the cases and run for the car

lines.text: The cruiser slows. An officer glances down at three men and a woman by a van in the rain. Rocco lifts a coffee cup in greeting. The cruiser rolls on.

lines.speaker: ROCCO
lines.text: No grenades. I'm not crazy. (He pockets the cash.) And tell your sister: if she ever mentions my court dates again, I'll stop being polite.
The cruiser's brake lights flare. Rocco's men scatter. You throw the cases into your trunk and Rocco shouts the last of the ammo boxes after you. You're gone before the cruiser turns.
You got the guns. Less ammunition than you paid for.
Day 1. Nila reads the list over the radio from her bed while you and Preethi push a cart through a huge outdoor store.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Red Lake in November can drop below minus thirty at night. Phones die in the cold. The cell signal ends before Red Lake does. Do not drink any water up there you didn't filter yourself. Ever.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Ever, Anna.

puzzle.title: The shopping list
puzzle.prompt: Pick everything Nila would approve. Leave out what will get you killed or slow you down.

options.t: Trauma kit: tourniquets, chest seals, clotting gauze
A big cooler of bottled water from home
Winter tyres, chains, a shovel, two jerry cans

hints: Cotton kills in the cold: it holds water. Bottled water freezes and isn't needed if you filter.
Everything rated for cold, plus medical, navigation, survival, and the car. Nothing cotton, no bottled water.
puzzle.answerText: Everything except the cotton clothes and the cooler of bottled water.

lines.text: Now it all has to fit in the trunk.

puzzle.title: Pack the trunk
puzzle.prompt: Load the trunk in order, from the first thing in (bottom, back) to the last thing in (top, front).
items: Long gun cases, flat on the floor
Jerry cans and tools, wedged at the sides
Sleeping bags and tent, on top of the cases
Food crate, where you can reach it
Medical kit, last in, first out
hints: Heavy and flat at the bottom.
The thing you need fastest goes in last.
puzzle.answerText: Guns flat, heavy at the sides, soft on top, food reachable, medical last.

lines.text: At the curb, Amma presses a steel box into Preethi's hands.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Puliyodharai. Sudbury-ku munnadi saapdunga.
lines.subtitle: Tamarind rice. Eat it before Sudbury.

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Naanum varen.
lines.subtitle: I'm coming too.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Appa, venaam. Nila-va paathukkonga. Adhu dhaan unga velai.
lines.subtitle: No, Appa. Look after Nila. That's your job.

lines.text: Appa nods slowly and holds your face in both hands. He doesn't say anything. He doesn't have to.
Preethi gets in the passenger seat and puts on her seatbelt with great precision, the way she does when she's frightened.
Highway 401, then 400 north. Rock cuts and pine. At a Tom Portons near Parry Sound, a woman in a grey coat jumps up from her booth.

lines.speaker: WOMAN
lines.text: My bag! My laptop bag was right here!

puzzle.title: The Missing Laptop Bag
puzzle.prompt: Find it.

spots.text: A coffee, a half-eaten muffin, a notebook full of shorthand. Wet sneaker tracks lead from the booth to the side door.
He keeps glancing out at the parking lot, then at the woman, then at his phone.
She shows Preethi a tracker app. Her bag's tag: moving slowly, twenty metres away, in the lot.
Propped with a napkin. Outside, a rusty hatchback with two kids in it, laughing.

lines.text: Preethi taps on the hatchback window and gives the two boys a look she normally saves for doctors who prescribe the wrong dose. They hand the bag over without a word.

lines.speaker: WOMAN
lines.text: Thank you. Really. (beat) I'm Ivy.
Ivy Laurent, mid-thirties. She thanks you a little too carefully. She glances at your face like she's checking it against a photo. Then she leaves, heading north.
A tired roadside motel. Through the window, the lit-up Big Nickel. You eat Amma's puliyodharai cross-legged on the bed.
Your phone buzzes: "Unknown tracker detected travelling with you."

puzzle.title: The Uninvited Passenger
puzzle.prompt: Search the car in the cold.
puzzle.doneLabel: Decide what to do with it

spots.text: Salt, slush, nothing.
Your fingers go numb. Nothing.
Fries. A hair tie. Nothing.
Taped inside the spare tyre: a small black tracker the size of a coin. Someone put this here in Windsor.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Smash it?

fx.toast: Whoever's watching knows you found it.

choices.label: Stick it on a transport truck heading east

fx.toast: Somewhere tonight, Northstar is following a load of frozen fries to Montreal.

lines.text: Day 2. Lake Superior opens up: huge, grey, empty, like the sea. Preethi presses her face to the window like a child.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: This is a lake? This is a LAKE?
At a Tom Portons in Sault Ste. Marie, the cashier is in tears. The staff tip jar has vanished.

puzzle.title: The Tip Jar
puzzle.prompt: There's a ring of coffee on the counter where the jar sat. There's a matching ring of coffee on the glove of a delivery driver unloading a crate of cups. What happened?

options.why: He's whistling and in no hurry. Thieves don't whistle.

options.t: The driver knocked it into his crate by accident

options.why: No customer touched that end of the counter.

puzzle.okMsg: The jar is in the crate of cups, full and unbroken. The cashier hugs Preethi.

lines.text: At the giant Canada goose statue in Wawa, snow starting. Ivy is there, photographing it.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: That's not a coincidence.
Ivy's room, two doors down. A laptop, maps, a bottle of wine she isn't drinking.

lines.speaker: IVY
lines.text: Your sister emailed me last year. From Greyhaven. I never wrote back. (beat) I'm sorry. I was hiding.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: From who?

lines.speaker: IVY
lines.text: From Northstar. I was a lab tech there for two years before I became a journalist. I saw what HX-7 does. I took a photo of one file, quit, and ran.
She draws a rough map of the surface buildings: gatehouse, office, loading dock, and a freight elevator that goes deeper than the mine maps say.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Put me on speaker. I want to ask her three things. In the right order.

puzzle.title: Nila's questions
puzzle.prompt: Nila builds an interview like a trap: easy questions first, the dangerous one last. Put the questions in Nila's order.
items: "What was your badge number at Northstar?" (easy to check)
"Who was your supervisor?" (a name we can verify)
"What colour is HX-7 in the vial?" (only a real tech would know)
"Why didn't you answer my email?" (the emotional one, last)
hints: Verifiable facts first.
The emotional question goes last, when she's relaxed.
puzzle.answerText: Badge, supervisor, the vial, then the email.

lines.speaker: IVY
lines.text: Badge 0417. Dr. Lund. Clear, with a faint blue tint under UV. (beat) And I didn't answer because I was scared, Nila. That's all. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: She's telling the truth. Mostly. (beat) Welcome to the team, Ivy.
Snow on the window. Preethi asleep. You awake, the handheld on the bedside table, tuned to your private frequency.
It crackles. A calm voice. The voice from the water tower in Greyhaven.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: Welcome to the north, Mani. Bring the file. (beat) And tell your sister: GH-01 is doing very well.
Preethi's eyes open in the dark.
End of Episode 1.
Wawa behind you. Ivy's dented hatchback ahead. Snow on the shoulders. Preethi has the Hades recording on repeat on her phone.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: "GH-01 is doing very well." He talks about her like a houseplant.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: That's what he wants you to feel. Angry people make mistakes. (cough) Don't give him that.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Nila, how are you feeling?

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Amma made me eat idli at six a.m. I'm feeling attacked. (beat) Drive, Anna.
A tiny town. A sign: Home of Winnie. A statue of a bear cub in a tree: the real bear that inspired Winnie-the-Pooh. A cluster of kids and a frazzled teacher.

lines.speaker: TEACHER
lines.text: Someone stole Winnie's scarf! The kids knitted it!
Red wool fibres on the bark of the statue's tree. Twigs and droppings under the gas station sign across the road. Through your binoculars: a nest on top of the sign, with a flash of red.

puzzle.title: Winnie's Scarf
puzzle.prompt: Who stole the scarf?

options.why: He's been inside all morning. The fibres are on the tree.
Then why is there red wool in a nest?
They're genuinely upset. And they can't reach the top of that sign.

lines.text: Preethi climbs the gas station ladder, retrieves the scarf, and is attacked by an extremely angry crow. The kids cheer. You film all of it.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anni lost a fight to a crow. Best day of my life.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: I WON. I have the scarf. I won.
At the pumps, a trucker with a grey beard and a CB radio watches you fill up.

lines.speaker: BIG LOU
lines.text: You folks headed west? Two black SUVs been running Highway 17 all week. No front plates. They stop where nobody stops. (He spits.) You hear "Kane" on channel nineteen, you get off the road.

The cable-stayed bridge over the Nipigon River. Superior's frozen edge. At sunset, the Sleeping Giant on the horizon across the bay. Preethi asks you to stop the car. You stand in the cold and watch it.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Nee bayappadriya?
lines.subtitle: Are you scared?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Romba.
lines.subtitle: Very. (beat) You?

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: I'm a pharmacist, Mani. Last month my biggest problem was a doctor's handwriting.
She puts her cold hand in your coat pocket with yours.

p2e2_okafor.place: Dr. Okafor's house, Thunder Bay · Night 3

lines.text: A warm house full of books. Dr. Grace Okafor, sixty, Nila's former criminology professor. Jollof rice and tea. Nila on speaker.

lines.speaker: DR. OKAFOR
lines.text: Nila was the best student I ever had, and she chose radio. I've never forgiven her.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: You came to my first show.

lines.speaker: DR. OKAFOR
lines.text: I came to judge it. (To you.) Tell me about the man.

puzzle.title: Build the profile
puzzle.prompt: Which conclusions does the evidence actually support? Choose all that apply.

options.t: He collects rare, dangerous animals → he needs control
He talked to Nila on the radio for months → he needs an audience
He sends gifts and taunts → he wants to seem generous, even while killing
He shot Victor at 600 metres → he's patient and practised
He hides in Red Lake → he's afraid of you

hints: He planned the poisoning months in advance. Not impulsive.
He isn't hiding. He gave you his address on a shipping label.
puzzle.answerText: Control, audience, false generosity, patience. Not fear. Not impulse.

lines.speaker: DR. OKAFOR
lines.text: He won't kill you from a distance, Mani. He'll want you in the room. He'll want to watch you choose.
She writes a name on a card.

lines.speaker: DR. OKAFOR
lines.text: Constable Rachel Dunn, OPP, Red Lake. She was my student too. Honest. Too honest for her own good.
Whiteout. Visibility ten metres. A transport truck jackknifed across both lanes, hazard lights blinking in the snow.

lines.speaker: BIG LOU
lines.text: …whoever's westbound by Ignace, that's no accident, I just came through—
Two black SUVs slide out of the snow behind you. Doors open. Men in white parkas with rifles.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: Mani. Just the file. Nobody has to freeze tonight.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Mani.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: I know.
You have seconds. The whiteout is your friend: if you move now, they haven't seen where you went.
First fight. In stealth you can take them one by one in the snow. If they spot you, it turns into a firefight.
A man on the roof of the jackknifed truck has seen the bodies. He opens up. The second SUV's driver tries to swing round to block your car.
Silence, except the wind. Ivy's hatchback is full of bullet holes. Ivy is crouched behind it, shaking, unhurt.
In the back of an SUV: a hard case stencilled NSB. Inside, in grey foam, six fragmentation grenades.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: (staring at it) These are grenades, Mani. Real grenades.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Then they're your grenades now. Put them in the trunk, Anni.
You each take two. The rest go in the trunk.
A motel by the highway. Preethi patches a graze on your arm. Neither of you sleeps much.
Morning. The car won't start. There's fuel on the snow under the engine.

puzzle.title: The Fuel Line
puzzle.prompt: Someone cut it. Find out who.

spots.text: Fresh boot prints. Big, new tread, crisp edges. They come from the motel office door, go to your car, and go back.
Cut with a blade. Clean. Not an accident, not the cold.
Tyler, twenties, wearing brand-new winter boots. There's $200 in crisp new bills in his tip cup.
Under a coffee cup: a Northstar Biologics business card.

lines.text: Tyler sees your face and goes white.

choices.label: Flip him: "Tell us who paid you, and we never met."

lines.text: An OPP cruiser takes Tyler away. He won't say a word. A man with a scar on his chin paid him, is all he'll admit. You lose an hour giving statements.

lines.speaker: TYLER
lines.text: A guy paid me. Big. Scar on his chin. Said you were thieves.

lines.speaker: TYLER
lines.text: Every Thursday night they run a convoy up 105. Northstar trucks. They stop for fuel at Ear Falls at nine. Three trucks, sometimes four. Please don't tell anyone I told you.
Ivy and you fix the fuel line with tape and a hose clamp from her trunk. She turns back toward Dryden to get her own car repaired: "I'll catch up in Red Lake."
Highway 105 narrows to two lanes. Forest on both sides for 170 km. No cell signal. Then Ear Falls: a dam, a gas station, a diner. Pie and coffee.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anna. Anni. Naan ungala nenachu romba perumai padaren.
lines.subtitle: I'm so proud of you both. (beat) Okay, that's enough emotions. Eat your pie.

lines.text: Snow falling. A gold-mining town on a frozen lake. Headframes against a violet sky. On the waterfront, the Norseman floatplane monument, frosted white.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: It's beautiful.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Everything up here is beautiful. That's what scares me.
The Northern Star Motel: twelve rooms, a coffee pot, a moose head over the desk. The owner, Bev Arsenault, reading glasses on her head, eyes your long cases.

lines.speaker: BEV
lines.text: Hunting?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Something like that.

lines.speaker: BEV
lines.text: Mm. Last person I had who was "something like that" was a girl from Toronto in 2024. Disappeared in the night, left her toothbrush. (She hands you a key.) Room seven. Checkout's at eleven. Murders are extra.
On the bed, a gift box with a silk ribbon. Preethi stops your hand.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Wait. (She checks it like a package at the pharmacy: no wires, no smell.) Okay.
Inside, on tissue paper: the shed skin of a golden lancehead. And a photo of Nila asleep in her hospital bed in Windsor, taken from inside her room. A card, in neat handwriting:
"Welcome to my town."

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Lighthouse! Nila! Answer me!
Static. Then Appa's voice, confused.

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Mani? Ava thoongittu irukkaa. Enna aachu?
lines.subtitle: Mani? She's sleeping. What happened?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Appa, room-la yaarachum vandhaangala?
lines.subtitle: Appa, has anyone been in the room?

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Oru doctor vandhaaru, kaalaila. Romba nalla manushan. Nila-ku flowers kondu vandhaaru.
lines.subtitle: A doctor came this morning. A very nice man. He brought Nila flowers.

lines.text: End of Episode 2.
You haven't slept. The radio on the bed. Ortiz's voice on it, from the highway.

lines.speaker: ORTIZ
lines.text: Took three days off. I'll sit outside her door in Windsor till you come home. Nobody brings her flowers but family. (beat) That's not a favour, Mani. I owe her.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Sam's here. He brought Tom Portons. Okay. Plan for today, Anna. Hospital, museum, rocks.

p2e3_hosp.place: Red Lake Margaret Cochenour Memorial Hospital

lines.text: A small, clean hospital, snow piled at the doors. Preethi introduces herself at the desk as a visiting hospital pharmacist from Windsor, which is true, and asks for the director. She gets Dr. Helen Marchetti, fifty-two, sharp, tired, stethoscope worn like a necklace.

lines.speaker: DR. MARCHETTI
lines.text: Windsor? You drove all this way to ask about my formulary?

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: I drove all this way because my sister-in-law has a cancer nobody understands. (She hands over Nila's panel.) This compound. Have you seen it?
Marchetti reads it. Closes her office door.

lines.speaker: DR. MARCHETTI
lines.text: Four times. Four men who did contract work at the Hayden Deep. All dead within five months. I sent samples to Winnipeg. The results came back "lost". Then Northstar donated a CT scanner to this hospital. (beat) I was told to stop asking.

puzzle.title: Five blood panels
puzzle.prompt: Preethi lays Nila's panel beside the four dead men's. Which findings do all five share? Choose all that apply.

options.t: Rising liver enzymes over three weeks

hints: Two things only: one compound, one pattern.
The peptide, and the liver enzymes.
puzzle.answerText: The peptide and the three-week rise in liver enzymes.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Same compound. Same pattern. Different start dates. (beat) Nila's three weeks behind the last man.

lines.speaker: DR. MARCHETTI
lines.text: (quietly) Then you have about three months. Maybe less.
Preethi doesn't move. You take her hand under the desk.
Gold pans, Norseman models, mine photographs. A volunteer docent, Mrs. Lindqvist, seventies, is delighted to have a visitor.

puzzle.title: The Hayden family
puzzle.prompt: Find what you can about the Haydens.

spots.text: Two prospectors grinning over a claim post. "Hayden brothers, Hayden Deep claim."
"Hayden Deep Mine, 1946–1991. At its peak, 300 men."
"Engineer R. Hayden leaves for southern Ontario dam project." The dam at Old Merrow. You know that name from a photo in a church basement in Greyhaven.
"Northstar Biologics — Mark Hayden, 2015."

lines.speaker: MRS. LINDQVIST
lines.text: Mark came home in 2015. Bought the old mine, built a big house way out past the Burn. Nobody's ever been invited.

lines.speaker: MRS. LINDQVIST
lines.text: His father too, they say. Though old Robert must be ninety if he's a day.
You write down "Robert".
A lot overlooking the mine buildings and headframe. A.Y. Jackson painted this view once. You and Preethi eat the last of Amma's puliyodharai in the car, heater running.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Three months.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Less.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: What if the cure doesn't exist?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Then Hades wouldn't send presents. You don't brag about a lock unless you have the key.
Cases of minerals: thousands of specimens, quartz, pyrite, real gold glinting under the lights. Somewhere in here are rocks from the Hayden Deep.

puzzle.title: The mineral collection
puzzle.prompt: Find the Hayden Deep specimens.

spots.text: Quartz veins, gold flecks. Not Hayden Deep.
Grey rock with pyrite. 1951.
A fist of quartz. 1958.
A beautiful gold specimen. The label is slightly crooked. Underneath, the edge of an older tag.

lines.text: You borrow the case magnifier. Under the Level 6 label, an older typed tag, mostly hidden.

puzzle.title: The hidden tag
puzzle.prompt: You can make out: "HAYDEN DEEP — LEV_L _ — 1962". The missing letter is obvious. The number is the last digit, partly scratched: it looks like a 6 with a tail, or a 9. The public maps show levels 1 to 6. What does the hidden tag say?
hints: If it were 6, why hide it under a label that says 6?
Level 9.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: The public mine maps show six levels.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: So there are three more nobody talks about. That's where the lab is, Anna.
A call to your phone brings you in. Constable Rachel Dunn, thirty-three, ponytail, notebook, very direct.

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: Two people from Windsor, long gun cases, asking about Northstar at the hospital and the museum. You know what that sounds like to me?

choices.label: "Some men shot at us near Ignace."

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: (writing) Why Northstar?

choices.label: Tell her about Nila's cancer and show the five blood panels
Show her the gun cases are locked

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: Grace taught me at Lakehead. (She closes her notebook.) I can't help you. I also can't arrest you for being sad.

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: Go home, Mr. Mani. Northstar pays half this town's wages. (beat) And if you don't go home, don't make me find you in a ditch.
Planes on skis on the frozen bay. A man in a heavy parka works on the engine of an old Norseman. Daniel Keeper, forty-five.

lines.speaker: DANIEL
lines.text: You're the couple asking about Hayden Deep. (beat) My cousin Joe worked there. He was the third one who died.

lines.speaker: DANIEL
lines.text: There's a stretch of land past the Burn nobody's allowed to fly over. Northstar got a restriction put on it. I know every lake around it.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Would you fly us?

lines.speaker: DANIEL
lines.text: When it's time. Not before. (He looks at the gun cases in your back seat.) And not with those pointed at my plane.
The nightly check-in. Nila reads the five blood panels back to you, voice thin.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: …so if the peptide binds in the liver first, then the three-week lag means he dosed me in the—
Her voice stops. A long electronic tone. Then voices in the room, running feet, the clatter of a falling tray. Then Amma.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Kanna! Nurses vandhurukkaanga, ava moochu—
lines.subtitle: Kanna! The nurses are here, her breathing—

lines.text: Static.
End of Episode 3.
You and Preethi sit on the floor by the radio, coats still on. You've packed the car to drive back to Windsor. Static for six hours.
Then a click.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: …Anna. Anni. Naan inga dhaan irukken.
lines.subtitle: I'm still here. (beat) They gave me oxygen. Ortiz yelled at a doctor. It was very funny.

lines.text: Preethi puts her face in her hands and cries.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Unpack the car. (beat) Find the man who dug Level 9.
A low wooden bar with a store at the back. Trophy fish on the walls. Miners on shift break, steam rising off their jackets.

puzzle.title: Asking around
puzzle.prompt: Ask the locals about the Hayden Deep.

spots.text: "Nobody at Northstar talks. They fly crews in from Winnipeg. Two weeks on, two off. They don't drink here."
"Old-timers say there's levels down there that never got mapped. Ghost stories, probably."
"Ask Sully. He's on McKenzie Island. He'll talk your ear off if you bring rye."

spots.t: A man at the end of the bar who won't look at you
spots.text: You ask him about Northstar. He finishes his beer in one swallow and leaves fast. Through the window, you see him make a phone call.

lines.text: The summer ferry is gone. A ploughed road of ice crosses the dark lake, marked by small evergreen trees stuck in the snow. Thin near the shore, where the current runs.
Halfway across: headlights behind you. Three snowmobiles, fast.

fx.toast: The ice booms and cracks under the tyres.

lines.text: The snowmobiles close in on both sides.
Preethi rolls down her window. Wind and snow pour in. She braces the shotgun on the door.
The third snowmobile is still on you as the island shore rushes up.
You hit the shore road at speed and fishtail into a snowbank. The snowmobile roars past and away into the dark.
A cabin crammed with mining junk, a wood stove, and a black cat named Nugget. "Sully" O'Rourke, seventy-eight, takes the rye before he takes your names.

lines.speaker: SULLY
lines.text: Hayden Deep. (He pours.) I dug Level Nine in seventy-four. Old Robert Hayden wanted a level nobody would ever see on a map. Said it was for "cold storage". I've dug gold for fifty years; you don't keep anything cold that far down. You keep it secret.
Sully refills his glass. "Ask me something."

choices.label: "What was Mark like as a boy?"

lines.speaker: SULLY
lines.text: Six of us. Nine months. Paid triple and told to forget it. We cut a vent raise up to the bush by Madsen so we could breathe down there. Nobody ever filled it in. I'd bet my cat on it.

lines.speaker: SULLY
lines.text: In the eighties. Three of the six of us. Lungs. Same as everybody else on that road. Company paid for the funerals. Very generous. Very quiet.

lines.speaker: SULLY
lines.text: Cold little thing. Used to catch garter snakes and keep them in jars on his windowsill. Watched them. Just watched them, for hours. Never let them go.
Sully turns over a calendar from 1974. On the back, in pencil: a hand-drawn map. Levels 6 to 9, the shafts, and a ventilation raise that comes up in the bush near Madsen.

lines.speaker: SULLY
lines.text: Only map there is. Take it. (beat) And son. The old man never died, you know. They say he lives out there with the boy.
You lay Sully's map over Ivy's surface sketch and the "Level 9" clue.

puzzle.title: The way in
puzzle.prompt: Ivy's map shows a guarded freight elevator. Sully's map shows the 1974 vent raise. Which way in is never on any modern plan?

options.why: It's on Ivy's map, and it's guarded.
That gets you in at the surface, not to Level 9.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: A side door nobody remembers. Every case has one. Good work, Anna.
You cross back on the marked road, slowly. Where the snowmobile went through, the ice is already freezing over. Preethi is silent.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: That man could have drowned.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: He was shooting at us.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: I know. (beat) I still want to remember that he could have drowned.
The office door is open. Bev is duct-taped to her desk chair, a bruise on her cheek, furious.

lines.speaker: BEV
lines.text: (as Preethi cuts the tape) Three of them. One with a scar. They wanted the Toronto girl.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Ivy's in Dryden—

lines.speaker: BEV
lines.text: She came back tonight. Two hours ago. Room four.
Room four: the door kicked in, the bed overturned, Ivy's laptop smashed. A drop of blood on the snow outside. Drag marks to where a vehicle waited.
Your radio clicks onto your channel.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: The journalist talks a lot when she's cold. (beat) Thursday, Mani. Bring the file. You can have whatever's left of her.
End of Episode 4.
Sully's map, Ivy's sketch and your notes spread on the bed. Nila on the radio, voice weak but precise.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Kane expects you at the front gate at midnight with the file. So you'll be there, Anna, and you won't. Ivy told me Northstar runs a supply convoy on Thursdays; it fuels at Ear Falls at nine.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Last truck, there's a gap between the pallets and the cab. You ride in. Anni takes the old ventilation raise near Madsen. You meet on Level 9.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: And if one of us gets caught?

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Then the other one is the plan. (beat) Bring me pictures. Bring me voices. Bring Ivy.

choices.label: Mani takes the M4, Preethi the shotgun
Preethi takes the M4, Mani the shotgun

lines.text: Three Northstar trucks fuelling under floodlights. The drivers are inside, buying coffee. You need to reach the last truck without being seen.
Between you and it: the ice machine, a parked snowplough, and twenty metres of bright concrete.

choices.label: Ice machine, then the snowplough's shadow, then the truck
Walk straight across like you belong there

lines.text: A driver comes out with his coffee and looks right at you. You freeze in the shadow of the truck.
The driver yells. You dive into the gap behind the cab as he comes round the corner with a flashlight. He swears, decides it was a raccoon, and climbs in. Your heart is louder than the engine.
You fold yourself into the gap behind the cab. Diesel and cold metal. The truck pulls out. North.
Deep snow. Preethi follows Sully's map by headlamp to a rusted steel cap in the trees: the 1974 ventilation raise. She cuts the padlock with Ruth's old bolt cutters.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Lighthouse, I'm at the side door.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Three hundred metres of ladder, Anni. Don't look down. Actually, look down. Watch where you put your feet.
Halfway down, a rung snaps under her boot.

choices.label: Grab the rail with both hands
Reach for the next rung down

lines.text: She drops a metre and catches a rung with one hand, slamming her knee into the rock. She hangs there, breathing. Then she climbs on.
A bat colony explodes past her face in the dark, hundreds of wings. She swears in Tamil, loudly. On the radio, Nila laughs weakly for the first time in days.
Two hundred metres to go.
The truck rolls through the gate. Floodlights, the headframe, a modern glass office bolted onto old brick. You slip out at the loading dock.
Three guards between you and the freight elevator. A locker room. Cameras.
Under the guard post bench: a hard case stencilled NSB. Grenades. And on a hook, a lab coat and an ID badge that opens the freight elevator to Level 6.
An alarm starts somewhere and stops. They'll be looking now. Under the guard post bench: a hard case stencilled NSB. Grenades. You take the elevator badge from a guard's belt.
Preethi drops from the last rung into warm air. You find the old ramp down from Level 6. You meet in a tunnel lit by white LEDs. She grabs your coat with both hands and doesn't say anything.
Then the tunnel opens.

A cavern of heated glass tanks, hundreds of them, in rows that disappear into the dark. In every tank, a golden lancehead. Robotic arms move from tank to tank, pinning the snakes and milking venom into vials. Freezers hum.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: (whispering) This is a farm. He's farming them.

puzzle.title: The venom farm
puzzle.prompt: Photograph everything.

spots.text: You count one row: forty-two tanks. There are twelve rows. Five hundred snakes from one island the size of a few city blocks.
A robotic arm pins a snake behind the head, presses its fangs over a membrane, and a gold drop runs into a vial. It moves to the next tank. And the next.
"HX-7 batch 41 → trial. HX-7C batch 3 → HOUSE ONLY."
Rows of labelled vials. Preethi reads them fast and takes one small box: antivenom. "One dose. If either of us gets bitten."

lines.text: A clean lab behind glass. A server terminal. You plug in the USB with the encrypted file from Greyhaven. Hades_contacts.enc.
It isn't a list of contacts. It's a key. The terminal asks for three fields to unlock the trial database.

puzzle.title: Unlock the database
puzzle.prompt: Pick the three fields the key expects. They come from the batch whiteboard, Victor's ledger, and the GH-01 delivery note.

options.t: Delivery note: Pike Point, the week of November 1

hints: Whiteboard, ledger, delivery note: one field from each.
41, H — 60%, and the Pike Point delivery.
puzzle.answerText: 41, H — 60%, and the Pike Point delivery date.

lines.text: The records open.

SUBJECT GH-01. Nila. "Route: drinking water. Location: Pike Point, Greyhaven. Progression: as expected." A scanned note in the margin, in neat handwriting: "Keep her alive until the brother comes. — M.H."
SUBJECTS RL-01 to RL-04: the four dead men. Joe Keeper is RL-03.
HX-7C (antidote): "Three doses. Stored at the house vault. Access: M.H. only."

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Nila. He wrote your name. In his own handwriting.
A long silence on the radio.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Then we have him on paper. Copy everything, Anna.
Behind a steel door marked SAMPLES −4°C: Ivy, zip-tied to a shelf, lips blue, a bruise over one eye. Preethi cuts her free and wraps her in her own parka.

lines.speaker: IVY
lines.text: (teeth chattering) I came back to warn you. They were in the parking lot.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: You're okay. I've got you. (She checks Ivy's pupils and fingers.) Early hypothermia. You'll keep your fingers.
Alarms. Red lights. A voice on the PA.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: Mani. You were supposed to come to the front door.
Guards pour into the venom farm between the tank rows. They've been waiting.
The old mine cage elevator. A slow ride up three hundred metres. Kane's men fire down the shaft from above.
You crash through a gap in the fence into the bush and run, Ivy between you. Then lights everywhere, red and blue. A ring of OPP cruisers on the access road. A megaphone.

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: Hands where I can see them. Both of you. Now.
Preethi looks at the Desert Eagle in her hand, then at you. Behind you, on the mine road, Kane's SUVs stop, turn, and drive calmly away.
End of Episode 5.
In the two seconds before the floodlights reach you, Preethi does something fast: she shoves both Desert Eagles and the long guns into a snowbank behind a spruce and kicks snow over them.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: (under her breath) Illegal guns, Mani. Ninaivirukkaa?
lines.subtitle: Remember?

lines.text: You step out with your hands up, Ivy between you. Dunn pats you down: a USB stick, a phone full of photographs, a pocket of dried fruit.
Dunn scrolls through the photos on your phone: the venom farm, the whiteboard, the GH-01 record. Ivy, wrapped in a blanket, gives a statement. Dunn's face changes.

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: You broke into a private facility. I should charge you both.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Charge me. But read page four first.
She reads it. "Keep her alive until the brother comes." She closes the laptop.

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: I can't get a warrant for Northstar on photos from a break-in. The judge in Kenora golfs with Hayden's lawyer. And half this town's mortgages are paid by that mine.

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: Officially, you were found lost on a snowmobile trail. (She slides the USB back.) Get your sister her medicine. And whatever you hid in that snowbank, I didn't see it.
No Nila. Instead, Amma's voice, and Appa beside her.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Kanna, Nila thoonguraa. Doctor sonnaaru, unconscious-nu. Konja naal aagalaam.
lines.subtitle: Kanna, Nila is sleeping. The doctor says she's unconscious. It may take a few days.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Aana naan inga irukken. Ava notes ellam en kitta irukku. Naan padichu solren.
lines.subtitle: But I'm here. I have all her notes. I'll read them to you.

lines.text: Preethi sits down slowly on the bed.
The radio clicks onto your channel.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: You took the journalist. So I took the old man.
A cough, then Sully's voice, angry: "Don't you come, son!" A thud.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: Starratt-Olsen. Midnight. Not the file this time, Mani. You. Walk in alone.

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Mani. Nila ezhudhinadhu inga irukku: "Kane fights near water. Kane likes high ground." Idhu ungalukku purinjadha?
lines.subtitle: Mani. Nila wrote this here: "Kane fights near water. Kane likes high ground." Does this make sense to you?

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Purinjudhu, Appa.
lines.subtitle: It does, Appa.

lines.text: First, the guns. In daylight, by the mine fence, with Northstar patrols driving the access road every ten minutes.

choices.label: Wait for a patrol to pass, then dig

lines.text: A patrol truck slows. You lie flat in the snow with a shotgun under you. The driver squints, shrugs, and drives on. Too close.
Everything is there under the snow. Cold, dry, loaded.
A near-ghost town. Empty houses with dark windows. A collapsed store. A little white church with a bell tower. Snow drifting through broken doors. A blizzard coming in off the lake.
You walk down the middle of the road alone, as you were told. Preethi isn't with you. She's already in the church bell tower with the long gun.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: Brave. Or stupid. Your wife's in the church, isn't she? (beat) That's fine. So's my sniper.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Nila ezhudhiyirukka: "Kane likes high ground."
lines.subtitle: Nila wrote: "Kane likes high ground."

lines.text: Preethi scans the town through her scope. Snow everywhere. Then: a puff of breath fog from the highest roof in town, the old hotel.
Three houses between you and the one with a light in the window. In the first, a frightened local hiding with his dog. You get them out the back door into the storm.
Three of Kane's men in the next two houses, waiting.
In the last house, Sully, tied to a kitchen chair, blood in his white hair, alive.

lines.speaker: SULLY
lines.text: (as you cut him loose) Told you not to come. (beat) Thank you for coming.
Outside, engines. Kane and four men, converging on the road.
Preethi comes down from the tower at a run. The two of you, behind an old truck, against Kane.
In Kane's abandoned truck: another hard case stencilled NSB. And a radio, still on Kane's channel.
The radio, after a day and a half of Amma's voice, clicks. A different breath on the line.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: …Anna… Anni… naan ellathaiyum kettukittu irundhen.
lines.subtitle: I heard everything.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Jonah got me a thermal image. Public satellite. North-west of the Burn there's only one heat source in four hundred square kilometres. A house. And behind it, something hot. Very hot.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: That's where the cure is.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: That's where he is. (beat) Call Daniel.
The Norseman on skis, engine roaring. Daniel at the controls, you beside him, Preethi behind with the guns. The town shrinks below.

lines.speaker: DANIEL
lines.text: Northstar got this airspace restricted. Not illegal to fly. Just unwise. (He grins.) Joe would've liked you.

The Burn: endless dark forest grown thick over old fire scars. A frozen private lake. On its far shore, a stone-and-glass mansion, steam rising from its roofs. Behind it, a black cone of rock breathing a column of white steam into the blue sky.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Is that a volcano?

lines.speaker: DANIEL
lines.text: Locals call it the Smoke. Geologists say it can't exist. (beat) It does anyway.
A sharp crack. A hole punches through the fuselage beside Preethi's head. A second crack. Oil sprays across the windshield. The engine coughs.

lines.speaker: DANIEL
lines.text: Rifle! From the ridge! Hold on!
Black smoke. The engine dies. In the silence, only wind. Daniel fights the stick, gliding toward a long frozen lake in the heart of the Burn. The ice rushes up.
Impact. White.
End of Episode 6.

The Norseman lies on its skis on the ice, one wing crumpled, the propeller bent. Steam from the engine. You pull yourself out of the cockpit. Preethi is already beside Daniel, whose leg is bent the wrong way below the knee.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Broken. Closed fracture. (To Daniel.) This will hurt very much.

lines.speaker: DANIEL
lines.text: You're a pharmacist, not a— AHH.

puzzle.title: Splint the leg
puzzle.prompt: Preethi talks you through it. Put the steps in order.
items: Check the foot for pulse and feeling
Gently straighten the leg into line
Pad around the leg with a jacket
Brace it with the seat strut, above and below the break
Tie it firm with paracord, not tight
hints: Check before and after.
Line, pad, brace, tie.
puzzle.answerText: Check, align, pad, brace, tie, check again.

lines.speaker: DANIEL
lines.text: (grey, sweating) Go. I'll fix the radio and keep the flare gun warm. When you're done, fire a green flare and I'll call it in. (beat) If you're not back by dark, I'm eating your sambar rice.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: …Anna… I'm here. I'm listening to them. I'm in their radio.
The tree line. Snowmobile engines somewhere. Two hunters in white camouflage working the shore, rifles slung. They don't know the plane came down this far west.
You take the first hunter's white parka, his toque and his radio. In the whites, from fifty metres, you're one of them.
Preethi looks you up and down. "You look like a marshmallow with a gun."
A ridge of black, dead trunks from the old fire, new pines thick below. A glint on the crest.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: Sniper. The same one who shot the plane.
You spot for her with the binoculars: "Three hundred. Wind left."
In the sniper's nest: another NSB grenade case, and a map of the hunters' patrol routes. A camp on the north trail. An ammo cabin in the ravine. A fire lookout tower where the routes meet.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: We split. Meet at the fire lookout.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: I hate this plan.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Nila made it.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: I hate it less.
A hunters' camp: tents, a fire, four men, two dogs. In the white parka you could walk right through it. Or bait the wolves you've heard all morning toward the meat rack.
A frozen creek and an old trapper's cabin, now an ammo dump. Three guards inside. Preethi can go under the cabin through the crawlspace, or through the front door with the shotgun.

You reach the old steel fire lookout tower at the same moment, from opposite sides. Preethi has a cut on her cheek and a stolen box of shells under her arm. You hold each other for exactly three seconds.
Beyond the lookout, a long lake to cross. Too many snowmobiles. Kane's voice on the hunters' channel, organising them.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anna… give me the hunter's radio.
You hold the captured radio against your own. Nila, in Windsor, listens for a full minute. Then she speaks on Kane's channel in Kane's clipped, flat voice.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: All units. Targets on the south lake. Intercept. Now.
Engines roar. Eight snowmobiles race out onto the south lake, where the current keeps the ice thin.
Preethi looks at you. She doesn't say anything.

choices.label: Warn them on their channel
choices.sub: They turn back. You lose your head start.

choices.label: Let it happen
choices.sub: The way to the lookout is clear.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Thin ice! South lake is thin ice! Turn back!
The snowmobiles skid, turn, scatter. Every one of them makes it back to shore. Now they know exactly where you are.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: …You were right. I'm glad you were right.
The ice opens. The lake takes machines and men. Then it's quiet, except for the wind.
Preethi doesn't say anything for a long time.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: …Anna, I'm sorry. I'm sorry I made you do that.
Kane, shoulder bandaged from Starratt-Olsen, waits at the top of the lookout with a heavy rifle.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: (shouting down) He said you'd come! He said you'd both come! He's got a bet on which of you dies first!
Close quarters on the switchback stairs. Two of Kane's men between you and the top.
Wind. Kane grabs Preethi as she comes up through the hatch and holds her out over the rail. You have one grenade and one magazine left.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: Drop it, or she flies.

choices.label: Throw the grenade off the far side of the platform

lines.text: Kane laughs and leans Preethi further out. Her boots scrape at nothing. No. Not like this.
Think. The grenade.

The grenade sails off the far side and bursts in the trees below. Kane's head snaps toward the blast. Preethi drives her elbow into his wounded shoulder and twists free. Kane staggers back against the rail, which gives way.
He hangs from the edge by one hand. You reach him.

lines.speaker: KANE
lines.text: He'll give you the cure. (A thin laugh.) He wants you to watch him choose which one.
His grip fails. He falls into the trees.

From the top of the tower, everything is visible. The frozen private lake below. On its far shore, the Hades Mansion, every window lit gold, steam pouring from vents on its roofs. Behind it, the Smoke breathes a white column into the violet sky.
In a glass-walled courtyard, something large and striped paces.
Preethi loads her last shells. You count the grenades.
The radio clicks onto your private channel. A calm voice, warm and pleased.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: Come in. Shoes off, please. I've made tea.
End of Episode 7.

Night. Minus thirty-five. You and Preethi cross the lake on foot in the hunters' whites, low and fast. The mansion grows ahead: stone walls, glass wings glowing green and gold, steam rising from copper vents. A thick pipe runs from the house up the slope of the Smoke.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: He heats it from the volcano. That's how his animals survive up here. (beat) Anna. Anni. Whatever's in that house, it's alive and it's hungry. Go slow.
Three ways in.

choices.label: The kennels: wolf-dogs and two guards
The boathouse roof, to a balcony
Grenade the generator shed and go in loud

lines.text: Wolf-dog hybrids pace a heated run. Two guards in the gatehouse with a thermos and a card game. Preethi crushes her sedatives into a hunk of the dogs' own meat.
The boathouse roof is coated in ice. Three metres of it to the balcony rail, with a twenty-metre drop to the frozen lake.

choices.label: Crawl on your stomach, spreading your weight

lines.text: Your boot slides. Preethi grabs your parka hood and hauls. You lie on the ice together, breathing, then crawl the rest.
The grenade blows the generator shed apart. Every light dies for thirty seconds, then flickers back on the geothermal backup. Guards run toward the noise.
Inside. Warm air, stone floors, the smell of wet earth and something like a zoo. Corridors lead off in every direction.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: He's in the study, upstairs. He's waiting. But the vault codes, the layout, anything you learn first, it all helps.

choices.label: Go up to the study
choices.lock: Explore at least three wings first

lines.text: A heated glass yard. A Siberian tiger lies on a warm rock, watching you with complete calm. Two guards patrol the corridor on the far side of the glass. Two gates: the inner gate into the yard, the outer gate into the guards' corridor. A lever for each.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: He keeps a tiger. Of course he keeps a tiger.

puzzle.title: The tiger
puzzle.prompt: You need the guards gone. Never fight the tiger.

options.t: Open the inner gate and walk through the yard
options.why: The tiger stands up. You step back very, very slowly and close the gate. Try something else.

options.t: Open the outer gate as the guards pass, and let the tiger out to them

options.why: No. Absolutely not. Preethi puts her hand on your gun.

puzzle.okMsg: The outer gate slides open. The guards see the tiger, and the tiger sees the guards. Everyone leaves the corridor very fast, in different directions.

lines.text: A jungle under glass, hot and dripping. Free-roaming golden lanceheads among the roots. A black mamba draped along the rafters. Poison dart frogs on the leaves like sweets.
Move slowly. Light every step. Don't touch the leaves.

choices.label: Slowly, flashlight on the path, step only on bare stone
Push through the leaves to save time

lines.text: A gold blur from the roots. Preethi cries out. Two punctures in her ankle above the boot.
Her hands are shaking but steady enough. She draws the antivenom from the Hayden Deep fridge and injects herself in the thigh. You hold her through the worst of it.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: (through her teeth) Good thing I'm a pharmacist.
At the far end of the conservatory, a service corridor and a ring of keys on a hook: the household keys, labelled. One says VAULT — MH.
A dark, warm saltwater pool. Things move under the surface: saltwater crocodiles. A catwalk crosses above, and a guard walks it back and forth.

choices.label: Cross behind him as he turns away
Cross toward him and take him down

lines.text: The guard turns. A shot cracks off the tiles. You hit him before he fires again and he goes over the rail. You don't look at the water. Neither does Preethi.
You cross in his shadow, step for step. He never turns. Below you, something large rolls lazily in the dark water.
Stuffed animals from every continent, glass eyes catching the light. A portrait gallery.
Robert Hayden in a long dark coat, 1978, beside the Merrow dam. A boy with a jar of snakes on a windowsill. A young man at a university lab bench. A plaque: "Hayden Family Trust — est. 1934."

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: The coat. It's the same coat.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Father and son. (beat) Anna. Which one have we been listening to?

Floor-to-ceiling equipment. Racks of recordings labelled by date: every one of Nila's broadcasts from Greyhaven, and her new show in Windsor. A wall of photos of Nila taken from a distance: at Pike Point, at the Windsor studio, asleep in hospital.
Nila, listening through your radio, hears her own voice playing on a loop in his room.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: …Anna. Burn it. All of it.

choices.label: Burn it: a flare into the tape racks
Take one tape and leave quietly

lines.text: A wood-panelled study. A fire. Tea in a china pot on a low table. A golden lancehead coiled on the desk like a sleeping cat. Behind the desk, for the first time, his face.
Mark Hayden, fifty-eight, silver-haired, soft-voiced, the long dark coat over a cashmere sweater.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: Shoes. (You don't move.) Fine. (He pours three cups.) Preethi, the pharmacist. Mani, the analyst. And Nila. I assume you're listening, Lighthouse.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: I'm listening, Mark.
He smiles, pleased, like a man hearing a favourite song.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: Your sister is the most interesting person I've ever listened to. A hundred nights of a voice in the dark, telling the truth to people who don't want it.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: Victor talked too much, so I stopped him. My father always said, never let the help speak at the table.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Why her?

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: She was the perfect subject: young, healthy, isolated, curious. She cost me Greyhaven. And I knew you'd come. (He looks at you.) Brothers always come.
He sets three identical glass vials on the desk, each with a white cap. A, B, C.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: One of these is HX-7C, the cure. The other two are HX-7, concentrated. One dose of that and she dies by morning. (beat) Give me the file, and choose. I'll let you take whichever one you pick. I want to see if you can save her.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: You'll just let us walk out.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: I'm a collector, Preethi. I collect moments.
Preethi asks for one minute and opens her pharmacy kit on his desk. He nods, delighted.
From the Hayden Deep files, she knows what HX-7C should do: a faint blue colour reaction, needle-shaped crystals, and slightly basic, around pH 7.6. She runs three tests on each vial.
Vial A: stays clear. Flat plate crystals. pH 6.8.
Vial B: faint blue. Needle crystals. pH 7.6.
Vial C: stays clear. Needle crystals. pH 7.4.

puzzle.title: The three vials
puzzle.prompt: Which vial is the cure?

options.why: NILA (on radio): Anni, A failed the colour test and the crystals are wrong. Check again.
NILA (on radio): Anni, C has the right crystals, but no blue, and the pH is low. He made it to fool you. Check again.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: (applauding softly) Oh, she's good. She's very good.
You hand over the USB. He plugs it into his laptop. Blank. Wiped.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: I erased it remotely this morning, Mark. You never needed it. You just wanted us here.
Hades looks at the empty screen for a long moment. Then he laughs, genuinely.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: I'm going to miss you, Lighthouse.
Outside, across the lake, a green flare climbs into the sky. Daniel. Then, far off, the thud of helicopter rotors.

Hades sighs and presses a button under the desk. Deep below the house, valves open. The pipes scream. Steam explodes from vents in every wing. Glass shatters in the conservatory. The animals are loose.
Steam, falling glass, alarms. Guards between you and the back terrace, where Hades is disappearing up the slope of the Smoke.
The black cone above you, hot under your boots despite the snow. Steam everywhere. Hades on a ledge, the golden lancehead around his arm, the coat whipping in the hot wind.

lines.speaker: HADES
lines.text: You know what my father will say? That I played with my food. (beat) He's right.

The ground cracks between you. A column of scalding steam erupts from the fissure with a roar. When it clears, the ledge is empty. A golden lancehead slides away over the rocks. The coat is gone. No body.
Neither of you fired. The Smoke took him.
An OPP helicopter lands on the ice, rotor wash blasting snow. Dunn jumps out, then two paramedics carrying Daniel on a stretcher, grinning, leg splinted.

lines.speaker: DUNN
lines.text: Your journalist sent the lab files to every newspaper in the country an hour ago. The judge in Kenora stopped golfing. (beat) Get in.
Preethi holds the vial in both hands inside her parka, against her heart, the whole flight.
Dr. Singh. Dr. Marchetti on a video call from Red Lake. Preethi with three pages of notes. The first dose.
A long, silent wait. Amma praying under her breath. Appa holding Nila's hand. Ortiz asleep in a plastic chair in the corridor.
Nila's eyes open.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anna… Anni… neenga romba late.
lines.subtitle: You two are very late.

lines.speaker: PREETHI
lines.text: (crying and laughing) Traffic.

Appa said it a year ago: "Come home for Pongal." The pongal pot boils over on the stove for luck and everyone shouts "Pongalo pongal!" A kolam at the door. Sugarcane in the corner. Amma and Appa in person this time.
Ortiz, Ruth and Jonah on a video call from Greyhaven. Daniel, Ivy and Dunn on another from Red Lake. Daniel's leg is in a cast covered in signatures.
Nila, thinner, hair short, laughing, back on her feet.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Appa, poana varusham nee sonna, Pongal-ku veetuku vaanu. (beat) Naan vandhutten.
lines.subtitle: Appa, last year you said come home for Pongal. (beat) I came.

lines.text: Preethi sits on the edge of the bed, holding something behind her back. She shows you a pregnancy test. Positive.
You stare at it. Then at her. Joy, so big it's quiet.
In the living room, Nila's old radio, switched off on the shelf, clicks to static on its own. An old man's voice, slow and amused:

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: Congratulations, Anni.
Silence. Nobody hears it.
A stone house somewhere you have never seen. Snow at the windows.
A very old man in a long dark coat, Robert Hayden, sits beside a hospital bed.
In the bed, burned and bandaged, Mark Hayden opens his eyes.
"You played with your food, Mark," the old man says. "Now we do it properly."
OUT OF TOWN WILL RETURN.
